cap: HIV becomes detectable in a fixed order: viral RNA at about 10 days, p24 antigen at about 2 to 3 weeks, and antibody at 3 to 4 weeks. A fourth-generation antigen/antibody immunoassay therefore turns positive earlier than an antibody-only test. The CDC algorithm confirms a reactive screen with an antibody differentiation assay and uses an HIV-1 RNA test to separate acute infection from a false-positive screen.
teach: A negative antibody-only test in the first weeks after exposure proves little, so a patient with the fever, rash and lymphadenopathy of acute retroviral syndrome is tested with a fourth-generation assay or an RNA test. In an infant born to a mother with HIV, maternal IgG makes antibody tests unreliable, so nucleic acid tests are used.
